title: Final distributed-execution seal

merge_window_decision.reason: DIST-G3, TEST-G3 and EXEC-G3 are independent final seals and remain separate.

promise_rows.text: Nested/delegated execution extends EXO/RUN rather than creating a parallel execution truth model.
Coordinator parent runs and delegated child runs have distinct canonical identities by default.
Each canonical run has one authoritative event-sequence producer.
Child semantic event run_id/event_id/sequence are immutable across forwarding.
Forwarding provenance lives in a typed transport envelope rather than rewriting semantic events.
Parent-run/node→child-run linkage is a first-class provider-neutral execution contract.
Federation-specific lineage metadata projects into the generic run-link contract.
SSH/chroot/PRoot/OCI delegation uses the same run-link/event transport contract.
External event ingest is distinct from ordinary local publish and recovery replay.
External ingest is idempotent for byte/semantic-identical duplicate events.
Same event identity with different canonical payload is detected as equivocation.
Recovery replay retains its no-live-listener semantics.
Live forwarded ingest updates normal subscribers exactly once.
Per-origin sequence, not cross-host wall clock, is authoritative ordering.
No global total sequence is invented across concurrent child runs.
Parent/child causal relation is represented separately from event ordering.
Delegated process/node identity cannot collide merely because hosts reuse PIDs or local keys.
Whole-run ownership transfer, if retained, has an explicit atomic sequence-handoff contract.
Runner semantic adapters execute at the child origin.
Parent never reparses child human stdout to rediscover semantic tasks/tests.
Gradle/npm/.NET semantic child nodes survive provider boundaries unchanged.
Generic stdout markers cannot impersonate trusted semantic events.
Every provider offers a dedicated event side channel or durable cursor source.
Detached SSH can reconnect and catch up from a durable origin journal.
Forwarding uses at-least-once delivery plus event-identity idempotency.
Forwarding tracks acknowledged origin sequence and detects gaps.
Gap catch-up uses the origin RUN journal rather than reconstructed presentation state.
Final child snapshot/event cursor are reconciled and integrity-checked.
A DelegatedExecutionReceipt records transport, child run, event range and terminal reconciliation.
Transport/event delivery health is separate from child execution status.
Event-bridge failure is a secondary diagnostic unless execution truth itself is unavailable.
Known child failures cannot be suppressed by bridge/UI/storage failures.
Control request/ack is a separate typed channel from telemetry.
Cancellation remains available when the live event channel is degraded.
Canonical child terminal truth reconciles transport rc and child snapshot without contradictory status/exit combinations.
Sequential and parallel federation expose equivalent child semantic execution truth.
Parallel federation imports/query-exposes canonical child nodes rather than a lossy terminal projection.
Parallel child custom Tasker state ceases to be a separate long-term execution authority.
RUN V3 stores child run/event/evidence truth once; parent history stores links/references.
Provider staging/spool directories are temporary transport state with explicit cleanup ownership.
Run hierarchy query supports ancestors, descendants and subtree inspection.
UIX/TUI/Desktop consume the same generic run-link hierarchy.
Parent progress derives from child relation without flattening child nodes into parent-run identity.
Reused child runs are referenced historically and never replayed as newly executed.
Live, recovery-replayed, catch-up-replayed and historical-reused provenance are distinguishable in projection.
Ordinary semantic events are sanitized before crossing trust/process/host boundaries.
Protected raw evidence never traverses the ordinary semantic event bridge.
Event transport declares its content/sanitization class.
External stream authorization is bound to the planned child run and provider/attestation.
An event's descriptive `source` string is never security authority.
Nested forwarding has route/hop cycle protection.
Unknown future safe events can be preserved through transport/journal compatibility.
Parent/child versions negotiate forwarding protocol/schema capabilities.
Network I/O never runs synchronously under EventBus publish lock.
Forwarding uses a bounded asynchronous queue/spool.
Canonical semantic events are never silently dropped due to backpressure.
High-volume raw process output follows TUI-X stream/storage policy rather than unbounded event forwarding.
Child raw stream attachments remain independently queryable according to RUN retention.
Forwarding does not add a second per-event synchronous fsync path.
Event delivery metrics/health never become a competing execution status model.
Parent machine output exposes child links and transport health without duplicating child history.
Parent final summary can identify a failed nested child and drill into its canonical run evidence.
Repository/target/provider identity remains attached to child-run linkage across remote transport.
Federation final child attestation and live event stream use the same planned identity boundary.
SSH worker/disconnected tmux event catch-up is provider-neutral at the semantic layer.
Chroot/PRoot local bridges preserve the same semantic event identities as SSH/federation.
Output/presentation flags never change delegated event identity or selection.
Event bridge lifecycle is idempotent across retry/reconnect/shutdown.
Permanent tests cover duplicate-equivalent vs duplicate-conflicting events.
Permanent tests cover sequential/parallel federation topology parity.
Permanent tests cover disconnect/reconnect gap replay.
Permanent tests cover delegated-event secret safety.
Permanent tests cover mixed-version/unknown event compatibility.
Permanent tests cover sustained high-volume/backpressure behavior.
Devtool dogfoods nested forwarding across federation, SSH and local delegated providers.
No nested-specific scheduler, RunStore, UI truth store or semantic parser is introduced.
RER reuse semantics integrate with child links without fake execution events.
COPY secondary-failure isolation applies to event transport/finalization failures.
TUI-X safe semantic stream contracts are reused instead of duplicated.
Host V2 provider/transport identity is referenced instead of reinvented by the event bridge.
Gradle V2 receipts/semantic nodes remain intact through delegation.
Federation parent dependency scheduling consumes reconciled canonical child terminal truth.
Final delegated-execution seal performs promise-by-promise lineage, ordering, redaction and parity checks.
Final architecture can follow one event from its origin child process through transport, RUN storage, parent hierarchy and every UI without changing its semantic identity.

Existing SSH-01 adaptive workspace/result transport, remote environment policy, multiplexing and worker preparation remain consumed substrate; DIST does not duplicate them as a second transport stack.

Existing SSH-02 persistent stdout/stderr, sessions/runs/output/follow, managed ssh exec, recovery and artifact-return lifecycle remain authoritative host-transport/runtime history features and are linked to, not replaced by, semantic event forwarding.

Existing SSH-03 known_hosts trust, GC, capacity qualification, deep doctor and lifecycle hardening remain authoritative provider qualification/cleanup inputs; semantic forwarding consumes their identities and safety decisions.

Existing GIT-FRX parent/child repository lineage, frozen-source identity, typed contract identity, hierarchical federation, cancellation/recovery and provider placement remain canonical federation inputs to DelegationLink.

Existing GIT-FRX Git-bundle transport and remote repository/config/source attestation remain source-materialization authorities; the event bridge binds to their attestation evidence instead of inventing repository trust.

Existing final federated provenance/seal evidence remains authoritative; DIST contributes event-delivery/child-reconciliation evidence references rather than creating a competing campaign seal format.
LIFE-qualified remote artifact, repository-pack, cleanup and signing requests travel through DIST as typed envelopes whose semantic object identity remains LIFE-owned.

Signing and other secret-bearing remote operations use explicit private transport channels; raw secret values never enter EventTransportEnvelope, ordinary semantic events, shell argv or serialized wrapper command text.

Resolved ToolInvocation/ToolArgumentBinding passthrough is finalized by EXEC/ENV before provider wrapping; DIST preserves exact argv boundaries across SSH/chroot/PRoot/OCI and never broadcasts ambiguous raw tails.
Remote Android execution resolves/records environment and device/artifact identities through ENV/ANDROID and forwards only those canonical references through delegation lineage.
Remote/instrumented test semantics originate at the child and preserve canonical TestResult/TestRunReceipt identities; DIST transports links/evidence but never reparses human output into test truth.
Provider staging/spool/event-cursor state has explicit LIFE cleanup ownership and may be reclaimed only after canonical RUN import/reconciliation and required recovery/reference checks.
Presentation flags and surfaces may change projection only; they cannot alter child selection, event identity, forwarding, control, reconciliation, passthrough binding or provider placement.
Mixed-version forwarding has an explicit capability-negotiation/degradation contract that distinguishes safely preservable unknown events from semantics that require fail-closed incompatibility.

DIST-X01 through DIST-X04 may run bounded targeted validation for changed non-Gradle boundaries; Gradle-related implementation validation is deferred. DIST-G1, DIST-G2 and DIST-G3 remain separate authoritative Devtool validation overlays, and `--no-validate` remains valid when no meaningful non-Gradle targeted check exists.

Every DIST implementation overlay retains the before-commit editable-install refresh hook so subsequent overlays and gates exercise the transaction candidate Devtool rather than a stale installed CLI.
DIST-G1 proves identity, equivocation protection, bounded forwarding, cursor/gap recovery, terminal reconciliation and sequential/parallel federation parity from fresh processes.

DIST-G2 proves provider parity across local subprocess, chroot, PRoot/OCI, SSH foreground, SSH detached/reconnect and nested federation, including control acknowledgements and hierarchy/retention behavior.

Before DIST-G3 every NEST-P001..NEST-P084 source promise and all 157 source regression cases have explicit evidence/disposition; historical SSH/FRX qualification contracts consumed by M007 are mapped rather than silently reimplemented or dropped.

DIST-G3 proves one event can be followed unchanged from origin child execution through provider transport, external ingest, canonical RUN storage, terminal reconciliation and parent hierarchy into machine/CLI/TUI/Desktop projections while preserving source identity and primary failure truth.

authoritative_final_proof: one child semantic event retains run_id/event_id/sequence/payload digest across origin journal, EventTransportEnvelope, external ingest and canonical RUN event store
terminal failed child truth reconciles without being replaced by transport/projection status
parent hierarchy retains canonical child run/delegation relation rather than flattening child nodes
machine/shared UI/TUI/Desktop projection inputs retain child canonical identity without creating a second truth store
reused child projection remains historical and never fabricates live replay
G2 provider parity remains closed across local, federation, chroot, PRoot/OCI and SSH foreground/detached classes
